what_it_measured.text: Reinforcing Lipid A Acylation on the Cell Surface of Acinetobacter baumannii Promotes Cationic Antimicrobial Peptide Resistance and Desiccation Survival

dose.text: Increasing concentrations of the C18G CAMP facilitated concentration-dependent killing in all A. baumannii strains.
A. baumannii strains were incubated with the indicated concentrations of the mammalian CAMP, C18G (A), polymyxin A (B), or polymyxin E (C) for 2 h.

endpoint.text: Survival of each strain was assessed by the relative loss of CFU compared to the wild type.

reported_results.text: Addition of the hydroxyl group to lipid A (red) results in a lipid A at m/z 1,530.96.

Importantly, the lpxMAb mutant displayed increased sensitivity to C18G, where a 1,000-fold decrease in the number of CFU per milliliter was recovered at a concentration of 10 μg/ml compared to the wild-type strain.

Following desiccation, bacterial CFUs were recovered for all strains except for the A. baumannii ⌬lpxMAb strain, for which no viable cells were recovered at either cell density tested, indicating a >1,000-fold decrease in CFU (Fig. 8A and Fig.
